body:
Found by the work on #3588 (PR for `band_reach`). Refs #3567, #3577.

## What happens
The tangency law (b), `section::tangency` in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` (about lines 74-147), takes one island slice for each move. The slice is at `min(from.z, to.z) + lift` (`section.rs:96`), through `Rest::islands_at`. The island cache (`rest.rs:146-157`) keys on the exact bits of Z. A ramp entry has a different Z at each move, so each move pays one full slice of the model.

Measured by the worker of #3567 in debug, on `pocket_pass_start::fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` with PR #3577: tangency takes 34.7 s for 2232 moves that are not planar (about 15 ms for each slice). Planning takes 0.21 s.

#3588 fixes the cost of `band_reach` only. `band_reach` uses the same slices; for a flat cutter (`lift` 0) on a descending ramp they are the same cache keys, so the slice cost is paid one time, in tangency.

## Why this needs its own design
The slice itself is the cost, not the use of it. Each plane gives a different Region: a face of two triangles crosses each plane at a different point. A reuse of one slice for a Z interval, or a snap of the key, changes the section that the law judges. That is a change of a gouge check, under the safety floor.

Possible directions (not decided):
- Slice incrementally: sort the facets by Z span, and keep the active set between two planes.
- Prove that two planes with no facet vertex between them give the same verdict for the law, and reuse the slice for them.
- Measure the release build first: if it is seconds there, lower the priority.

## Done means
- A path with about 2000 distinct cut Z values verifies tangency in a time that does not grow with moves x slice cost, or the release time is measured and found small.
- The findings of the tangency law do not change on the existing tests (an equivalence test against the old law).
